blocks.body: Labs 02 and 03 and TC-02 taught the radio, a 2-meter offset example, and a first call. This lab is the rest of the operating: CQ, a 70-centimeter offset, reverse, tones, a directed net, a short formal message, and a public-service role. No microphone is required. Offsets shown here are common United States examples, not a rule for every repeater.

config.doneText: Simplex is one frequency, and the call included your call sign.
CQ asks any station for a contact. You listened, waited, identified, and answered.
You answered CQ with their call sign and yours.

blocks.body: A repeater output and input are separated by the offset. The sign can be plus or minus. Reverse listens on the input. DTMF is a keypad command. DMR still needs a talkgroup and a color code after the frequency is set.

Use the repeater the way you just configured it, then deal with interference, join a directed net, and pass a message without rewriting it. QRM is interference from other stations. QSY means change frequency.

config.doneText: You called a known station, and you identified when you were just listening.
You moved a crowded contact, left the linked repeater for a long chat, and turned the gain down when audio dropped out.
You waited for net control, checked in, and stayed off the frequency for priority traffic.
You passed the text you were given, and the check matched the word count.

blocks.prompt: Why is listening and understanding how a frequency is being used often more important than immediately transmitting?
blocks.reference: A transmission lands on whatever is already there: a contact, a net, a linked repeater, or a priority message. Listening tells you whether the frequency is free, whether someone is running a directed net, and whether your call should be CQ, a call to one station, or silence. Transmitting first can cover that use. Identification does not undo the interference.

blocks.body: These are Radio Lab practice items about the operating you just did. They are not the official pool.

questions.stem: You want any phone station, you are on simplex, and the frequency is quiet. What does transmitting CQ with your call sign do?
choices: It asks any station to answer you
It silently tests the repeater
It enrolls you in a net
questions.why: CQ is a general call. Your call sign tells the answering station who is calling. You still listen before and after it.

questions.stem: A station is calling CQ. How do you answer in this lab?
choices: Their call sign, then yours
Another CQ on the same frequency
A silent key-up so they see the meter move
questions.why: The answer names them and then names you. A second CQ covers the station that already asked for a call.

questions.stem: This lab's 70-centimeter example uses a 5 MHz offset. What is the right way to treat that number?
choices: As a common United States example, checked against the repeater you are using
As the offset of every repeater on Earth
As the bandwidth of an FM voice signal
questions.why: The offset is the split between input and output. Five megahertz is common on 70 centimeters in the United States. The repeater listing still wins.

questions.stem: You turn on reverse. What changes?
choices: You listen on the repeater input
The transmitter power increases
The CTCSS tone becomes DTMF
questions.why: Reverse lets you hear stations on the input. It does not add power and it does not change the tone type.

questions.stem: You press one key and the model shows two tones at the same time. What is that keypad for here?
choices: A short command, such as a repeater control
The continuous tone that opens a CTCSS squelch
A substitute for your call sign
questions.why: DTMF is the pair of tones. CTCSS is the separate low tone that rides with your voice to open a receiver.

questions.stem: A DMR radio is on the repeater frequency and you still are not in the conversation. What else did this lab require?
choices: A talkgroup and a matching color code
More transmitter power only
Calling CQ in voice
questions.why: Digital voice uses configuration beyond the frequency. The talkgroup selects the group. The color code is the digital access code. A code plug stores those settings.

questions.stem: Two stations are interfering with each other on one frequency. Which Q signal names that problem?
choices: QRM
QSY
A signal that means the net is closed
questions.why: QRM is interference from other stations. QSY means you are changing frequency, which is often the cure.

questions.stem: You earned a Technician license yesterday. Which statement matches this lab?
choices: The license does not enroll you in RACES or ARES
The license makes you a civil-defense station
Part 97 stops applying when a net uses the word emergency
questions.why: RACES needs a civil-defense enrollment. ARES is a voluntary registration of amateurs. Part 97 still applies during the net. The license is not either membership.

blocks.body: Public-service operating mission. An organized race is already on the air. Configure the radio, join the directed net, pass a short message, deal with interference, and leave the frequency clear for a priority call.

config.doneText: You joined the net that existed, used the listed repeater settings, passed the message as written, and stood by for priority traffic.

blocks.body: Formal voice traffic is not the only way a message moves.
